summary: Private install: CPU/memory saturation alerts became noisy after upgrade (thresholds too tight for inference pods)
description:
Issue summary:
After upgrading HelioBank’s Redwood Private cluster, Prometheus began firing frequent CPU/memory-related alerts for the serving runtime even though application-level latency/error SLOs remained healthy. Customer reports alert fatigue and requests guidance on tuning + confirmation of whether this is a known issue with the minimum observability pack.

Impact:
- High-volume alert noise (non-actionable) causing on-call fatigue.
- No customer-facing outage reported; inference remained available.

Customer context:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (on-prem, air-gapped)
- Upgrade: Redwood Private 1.9.4 -> 1.10.0 (same hardware footprint)
- Observability: bundled Prometheus + Grafana; alerts routed to OpsGenie

What’s firing (examples provided by customer):
- RedwoodServingHighCPUUtilization (warning) flapping during normal batch spikes
- RedwoodServingMemoryWorkingSetHigh (warning) constantly firing on one model pool
- RedwoodServingPodOOMKilled (critical) fired once but no user impact (container restarted cleanly)

Notes / initial hypothesis:
- Thresholds in v1 rules are too aggressive for bursty inference workloads (continuous batching / tokenizer spikes). The alerts were intended as early indicators, but in practice are paging/ticketing too often post-upgrade.
- In this customer’s environment, runtime pods are configured with high CPU limits to allow short bursts; comparing utilization against limit makes the baseline look “high” even when the node is not saturated.

Request:
1) Provide recommended tuning parameters for Private installs.
2) Confirm whether we have a rule change queued to reduce noise by default.
3) Provide a safe workaround for air-gapped clusters (values override) until the next patch release can be applied.
comments: 2025-07-18 09:12 UTC - Dev Patel: Opened on behalf of HelioBank (Maya R., Platform Eng). They upgraded to 1.10.0 last night and are getting ~150 alerts/hour, mostly CPU/memory warnings on serving-runtime. Asking whether they should disable the new rules or if there’s an updated bundle.

2025-07-18 10:03 UTC - Rafael Mendes: Can you ask for: (1) a screenshot/export of firing alerts w/ labels, (2) pod resource requests/limits for serving-runtime, (3) Prometheus rule group name + pack version, (4) whether these are paging or ticket-only in their routing policy?

2025-07-18 12:21 UTC - Dev Patel: Customer provided details: Pack version reported by Helm values is observabilityPackVersion=0.4.0 (bundled with 1.10.0). Serving runtime: requests cpu=4, mem=16Gi; limits cpu=24, mem=32Gi. Alerts are routed as pages due to generic OpsGenie mapping (anything ‘warning’ -> page). They can change routing but prefer we adjust defaults / provide explicit guidance.

2025-07-18 14:05 UTC - Rafael Mendes: Reproduced in staging by applying similar requests/limits; CPU warnings fire during normal batching spikes. Our rule uses utilization vs limit with short window; recommend moving warnings to ticket-only + raise thresholds + add longer ‘for’. Also memory working set threshold should compare to request (or use node pressure signals) to avoid constant noise on large models.

2025-07-19 08:44 UTC - Tomáš Novák: +1. We should ensure annotations explicitly say “ticket-only” for warnings and reserve paging for sustained saturation + node pressure or error budget burn. Customer’s paging policy is mapping all warnings to page; we should document that mapping is not recommended.

2025-07-19 11:30 UTC - Rafael Mendes: Proposed immediate tuning for customer (values override): set CPU warning threshold to 0.90 with for=15m; set memory working set warning to 0.92 with for=20m; keep critical at 0.98 with for=10m; route OOMKilled to ticket unless it repeats (increase to ‘>0 in 30m’ AND ‘restarts > 2 in 30m’).

2025-07-20 16:02 UTC - Dev Patel: Sent customer workaround + routing guidance. They’ll implement in the next maintenance window and confirm. Asked if we can provide a patch so they don’t need a permanent fork of rules in their air-gapped bundle.

2025-07-21 09:18 UTC - Sergio Costa: We have a rules change in-flight to reduce noise for Private: increase thresholds, add ‘for’ durations, and change some warnings to be disabled-by-default. Linking PRs: observability-pack PR-18372 and PR-18356 (includes runbook links + severity mapping updates). Helm wiring in redwood-helm-charts PR-18405 will allow customer overrides without patching manifests.

2025-07-22 13:40 UTC - Dev Patel: Customer confirmed improvement after tuning: CPU warnings reduced from ~150/hour to <5/hour; memory working set warning still firing on one pool during model warm-up but no longer paging after routing change. They requested a recommended default routing policy snippet for warning vs critical.

2025-07-23 08:55 UTC - Rafael Mendes: Closing as resolved with workaround + fix queued. Follow-up: ensure next Private bundle includes updated rules and docs explicitly state recommended alert routing (warning->ticket, critical->page) and that CPU/memory utilization warnings are early indicators, not necessarily customer-impacting.
workaround:
Customer-side tuning (air-gapped friendly): override alert thresholds + durations via Helm values, and adjust alert routing so warnings are ticket-only.

Suggested values override (example; names may differ by chart version):
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.cpu.utilizationWarningThreshold: "0.90"
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.cpu.utilizationWarningFor: "15m"
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.memory.workingSetWarningThreshold: "0.92"
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.memory.workingSetWarningFor: "20m"
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.cpu.utilizationCriticalThreshold: "0.98"
- observabilityPack.alerts.runtime.cpu.utilizationCriticalFor: "10m"

Routing guidance:
- Treat warning alerts as ticket-only by default.
- Page only on critical saturation that is sustained OR correlated with user-impact signals (latency/error SLO burn, node pressure, repeated OOM/restart loops).
resolution:
Resolved via guidance + confirmed customer mitigation. Engineering fix is tracked via rules updates to reduce default noise (raise thresholds, add ‘for’ durations, improve OOM/restart correlation, add clearer annotations about paging vs ticketing) and chart wiring to make overrides first-class.

Planned fix landing:
- Updated rule defaults in observability-pack (see related PRs)
- Helm chart wiring to allow supported tuning without manifest edits

Customer outcome:
- Alert volume reduced to acceptable levels after applying overrides and adjusting routing policy; no further action required from Support until updated pack is available in their next upgrade.
next_steps:
1) Backport updated alert rules into the next Private patch bundle (release coordination).
2) Add explicit ‘Recommended alert routing policy’ section to Private day-2 runbook.
3) Validate in staging with high-limit/low-request configurations to ensure defaults remain low-noise.
4) Follow up with HelioBank after they adopt the patched bundle to confirm no regressions.
internal_notes: This was triggered by customer routing policy (warning->page) combined with aggressive default thresholds for inference workloads. We should treat this as both a docs gap (routing guidance) and a rules calibration issue for Private where clusters vary widely in resource sizing. Ensure alert annotations include runbook link + “what to check first” per oncall feedback thread.
